secretName.description: The NAME of a secret, delivered as `secrets.source` says: `valkey/password`, `issuer/state-secret`. A value is never in the document.

url.description: An http or https URL with a host and no credentials: a password in a URL is a secret in the file, and a secret is named, never carried.

description: What an estate knows about one installation of sluis, from which `sluisctl render` and the Pulumi library write the service document and the policy document. A superset of the two: a section is under the key the document gives it, and the installation adds the shape it runs in and the AWS and OpenBao resources it is built on. Secrets are never in this file: a field ending in ...Secret holds the NAME of a secret, which `secrets` says how to deliver, and a field ending in ...File holds a path (a credential the platform mounts and rotates). Telemetry is the OTEL_* environment, not configuration.

access.description: The access model's tables (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md): the groups, the clients, the resources, the GitHub and Slack bindings. They are the policy document's, unchanged.

additionalProperties.description: A claims fragment: merged into the token (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md#claims).

claims.description: What a group adds to a token, by group.

client_documents.description: Admits clients that are not declared, by a document they serve about themselves. Off unless it names an origin.

groups.description: Which held groups beyond the requires pairs a token for it carries: `all`, or a list of things, families or names (docs/reference/sluis/policy.md#groups-in-a-token-scoping).

requires.description: The groups a caller must hold.

session.description: Every document client's refresh chains: `interactive` (a person at a browser, the installation's `lifetimes`) or `agent` (software that holds its refresh token and works in the background, the service's `lifetimes.agent`). Recorded on each chain when its authorization completes (docs/decisions/0040). Never read from a document: admit with `agent` only an origin whose documents its vendor controls.

additionalProperties.description: A client: who may be issued a token, and for what. Its id is the audience.

backchannel_logout_uri.description: Where a back-channel logout is posted.

description.description: One line about it on the sign-in page. Public.

display_name.description: What the sign-in page calls it. Public.

secret.description: For a confidential client: the name its secret is delivered under, or `{generate: true}` to have the issuer generate it and keep it with its credentials.

generate.description: Must be true; `generate: false` is refused.

session.description: Its refresh chains: `interactive` (a person at a browser, the installation's `lifetimes`) or `agent` (software that holds its refresh token and works in the background, the service's `lifetimes.agent`). Recorded on each chain when its authorization completes (docs/decisions/0040). Refused on an exchange client and, as `agent`, with `sign_in_exchange`.

apiVersion.description: Which version of which document this is. sluis.truvity.github.io/installation/v1 is what this build reads and writes.

apps.description: What an operator may make on the console.

Every GitHub App the installation declares, of every purpose: the link App, the catalogue Apps and the runner tiers (docs/guides/sluis/connect/github-apps-catalogue.md). A grant naming an undeclared group stops the service.

items.description: One App. A `catalogue` entry needs `org` and `permissions`; a `runner` entry needs `tier` and declares nothing of a catalogue App's; the `link` entry has the id `link`.

events.description: Webhook events the App subscribes to. They are delivered only to an App that declares a `webhook`.

export.description: Place the installed App's key at `external/github/<id>` for a consumer to read. Unset keeps it internal. A runner App is always exported.

grants.description: Who may ask for tokens of it, and for how much.

permissions.description: Permission name to level: read, write or admin.

id.description: The App's key in storage, unique, never changes. `link` for the link App; for a catalogue App [a-z0-9-], at most 32, not beginning `runner-`; a runner entry may leave it out (`runner-<tier>`, and `runner-<tier>-<org>` with an `org`).

labels.description: At most 16 short lower-case labels, key to value, kept on the App's record for a reader that selects Apps by them.

org.description: The organisation a catalogue App is created under (required for it), or the only organisation of a runner entry (no `org` offers the tier in every organisation). The link App's owner.

permissions.description: Permission name to level: read, write or admin.

purpose.description: What the App is for: `link` is the App that links a person's GitHub account, `catalogue` an App an operator creates and installs from the console, `runner` the tier an operator may create a runner App for.

tier.description: A runner entry's tier: lower-case letters, digits and dashes, at most 16.

webhook.description: Where GitHub delivers the App's events: exactly one of `url` and `kargo`. Needs non-empty `events`; set `export: true` so a consumer can read the secret. The secret is generated by this service, set on GitHub right after the App is created, and kept at `external/github/<id>` as `webhook_secret`; it is rotated from the console, without overlap (docs/decisions/0041). An App created before this is declared cannot be switched to a webhook: GitHub has no API for that, so disconnect it and create it again.

kargo.description: A Kargo GitHub receiver. Kargo derives the receiver's path from its secret (`/github/<hex sha256(project + receiver + secret)>`), so the URL moves whenever the secret does.

project.description: The Kargo project; empty for a cluster-scoped receiver.

receiver.description: The receiver's name in the Kargo project.

url.description: The endpoint every delivery is POSTed to, e.g. Argo CD's `https://argocd.example/api/webhook`.

catalogue.description: DEPRECATED, removed in v1.77: declare each as a `purpose: catalogue` entry in `apps`. Read as those entries, with a warning.

items.description: One App: created under `org` from the console, and installed there.

events.description: Webhook events the App subscribes to. They are delivered only to an App that declares a `webhook`.

export.description: Place the installed App's key at `external/github/<id>` for a consumer to read. Unset keeps it internal. An id may not begin `runner-`.

grants.description: Who may ask for tokens of it, and for how much.

permissions.description: Permission name to level: read, write or admin.

org.description: The organisation it is created under.

An App created before this is declared cannot be switched to a webhook: GitHub has no API for that, so disconnect it and create it again.

project.description: The Kargo project; empty for a cluster-scoped receiver.

receiver.description: The receiver's name in the Kargo project.

url.description: The endpoint every delivery is POSTed to, e.g. Argo CD's `https://argocd.example/api/webhook`.

runnerTiers.description: DEPRECATED, removed in v1.77: declare a `purpose: runner` entry in `apps` for each tier. Read as those entries, with a warning.

catalogue.description: Every Slack App the installation declares (docs/guides/sluis/connect/slack-apps-catalogue.md). One for a workspace the policy does not declare stops the service.

items.description: One Slack App, created and installed from the console.

workspace.description: A key of the policy's slack.workspaces.

audit.description: The audit installation this service records to. Unset keeps the trail in the log only.

audience.description: The client whose audience the Audit page's tokens carry.

forwardedForTrustedHops.description: How many of the deployment's own proxies append to X-Forwarded-For; zero records the peer.

queryURL.description: The query service, for the console's Audit page. Its own setting: it needs no `writer`, so the page works with the `sqs` and `log` sinks. A path prefix (`https://audit.example/sluis`) is kept and the procedure path appended.

tokenFile.description: This workload's projected service-account token, presented on every call.

aws.description: The AWS account and the resources the installation is built on. Each resource named here becomes the adapter setting that uses it (`state` the table, `blobs` the bucket, `audit` the queue), unless `adapters` names that concern.

auditQueueURL.description: The audit ingest queue the `sqs` audit adapter sends to.

bucket.description: The S3 bucket of the `s3` blobs adapter.

functionName.description: The function's name (shape `lambda`), which the `invoke` trigger names for a run-now. Default `sluis`; the Pulumi library supplies its own `FunctionName`.

region.description: The region of the resources and of the SSM parameters. Required for shape `lambda`.

table.description: The DynamoDB table of the `dynamodb` state adapter.

cloudflare.description: sluis as the STS for Cloudflare API tokens and R2 credentials (docs/guides/sluis/cloudflare-tokens.md). Cloudflare has no web-identity federation, so sluis holds one minter credential per account and hands out short-lived account tokens cloned from a DISABLED prototype token. Needs the ssm secrets source. Unset is off.

minter.description: The internal address of the minter credential, `internal/cloudflare/<account>/minter`: a cloudflare-minter/v1 document holding an account token that has Account API Tokens Read and Edit and nothing else. It is never an external address: nobody but sluis is granted it.

accounts.description: The Cloudflare accounts sluis mints in, by the name presets use.

forbiddenPermissionGroups.description: Permission groups, by the name Cloudflare lists them under, that a prototype may never grant, IN ADDITION to the built-in list: Account API Tokens Edit (Write), Billing, Account Settings, Memberships, and Access: Organizations, Identity Providers, and Groups. The built-in list is the only thing between the minter and everything its creator could do, so it cannot be shortened by configuration, only extended.

group.description: A group of this policy: every holder may ask, a person from the console or `sluisctl`, a CI job through the exchange. A CI job is a group declared with `github` matchers.

additionalProperties.description: One preset: a prototype token and how long its clones live.

description.description: What the preset is for. Shown by the console and `sluisctl whoami`.

endpoint.description: Makes this an R2 preset: the S3 endpoint of the account (`https://<account-id>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com`, or `https://<account-id>.eu.r2.cloudflarestorage.com` for an EU jurisdiction). The stored document then holds an access key and secret instead of a token.

lifetime.description: How long each minted token lives: its `expires_on`. At least 1m, at most 24h. Past it sluis deletes the token in Cloudflare.

prototype.description: The id of the prototype: an account token in Cloudflare that is DISABLED and whose policies and condition are the preset's rights. An active prototype is refused (it would be a usable token that never expires), and so is one granting Account API Tokens Edit, Billing, Account Settings, Memberships or Access identity providers. It is read at every mint, so editing it applies at the next rotation.

rotation.description: How often the stored token is replaced. At least 1m and shorter than `lifetime`: `lifetime - rotation` is the time consumers have to pick up a new token.

presets.description: What may be minted, by name (a DNS label). The name is in the external address, `external/cloudflare/<preset>`, and in the name of every token minted for it.

remote.description: Where the minter is when it is not this process: the on-demand token exchange calls the Cloudflare module there (docs/decisions/0071), and this document then declares no `accounts` or `presets`. Set exactly one of `function` and `url`. Unset keeps the minter in this process.

audience.description: The audience of that token. The module's name, `cloudflare`, when unset.

function.description: The module's Lambda function, name or ARN. It is invoked through its `live-issuer` alias.

tokenFile.description: Where the projected token is mounted. `/var/run/secrets/sluis/cloudflare/token` when unset.

url.description: The module's Kubernetes Service. A call carries the pod's projected ServiceAccount token.

serve.description: Makes the Cloudflare module answer other modules' calls (docs/decisions/0071): the issuer's token exchange when its `remote` names this module. On Kubernetes the module listens on `address` and accepts a call that carries a projected ServiceAccount token minted for `audience`, checked with a TokenReview; any other call is a 401. On Lambda the function answers `rpc` events, and IAM decides who may invoke it. Needs `presets`; not with `remote`. Unset serves nothing.

address.description: The listener on Kubernetes, `host:port`; it also answers `GET /healthz`. Unused on Lambda.

audience.description: The audience a caller's token must be minted for. The module's name, `cloudflare`, when unset.

cluster.description: Names the cluster the installation runs on in a ServiceAccount's subject (the service document's `cluster`).

console.description: Where the console is published, for the sign-in that starts there.

awsAudience.description: The audience an AWS role's web identity token must be minted for to be a bearer at the console (a Lambda controller). Its own, distinct from the AWS federation file's, so a token for token exchange is no proof here and the reverse. Default `<issuerURL>/console`.

client.description: The client id the console signs in as.

origin.description: The console's origin, when it is not the issuer's.

controllers.description: The controllers this installation runs, each in its own loop; an absent one is off. A section's own keys go to the service document's `controllers`; `enabledOrgs` and `enabledWorkspaces` go to the policy document's.

github.description: The GitHub controller: makes each GitHub organisation's teams match the policy's github table.

appsDir.description: One file per connected organisation: its App's credentials. Read only with `ports.adapter: legacy`; with another adapter they are on the State port.

console.description: How the controller proves itself to the console, when the pod's `tokenFile` is not the way.

aws.description: The function role's AWS outbound web identity token (`sts:GetWebIdentityToken`), re-minted every four minutes. The console's issuer must federate the account, and its policy must declare an `aws` matcher for the role.

audience.description: The audience requested from STS. It must equal `console.awsAudience` (default `<issuerURL>/console`), NOT the audience of the issuer's AWS federation file.

consoleURL.description: The console's API, which answers who holds a group. Unset is `publicURL`. On Kubernetes it is this release's own Service, which the chart writes.

enabledOrgs.description: The organisations the controller may CHANGE (the policy document's `controllers.github.enabledOrgs`). Each must be bound by `access.github`. The rest are derived every pass and left alone.

recordsDir.description: The console's records, mounted. Read only with `ports.adapter: legacy`.

tokenFile.description: This pod's projected ServiceAccount token, presented to the console and read afresh on every call.

slack.description: The Slack controller: makes each Slack workspace's user groups match the policy's slack table.

console.description: How the controller proves itself to the console, when the pod's `tokenFile` is not the way.

aws.description: The function role's AWS outbound web identity token (`sts:GetWebIdentityToken`), re-minted every four minutes. The console's issuer must federate the account, and its policy must declare an `aws` matcher for the role.

audience.description: The audience requested from STS. It must equal `console.awsAudience` (default `<issuerURL>/console`), NOT the audience of the issuer's AWS federation file.

consoleURL.description: The console's API, which answers who holds a group. Unset is `publicURL`. On Kubernetes it is this release's own Service, which the chart writes.

credentialsDir.description: One file per connected workspace: the app's credentials and its bot token. Read only with `ports.adapter: legacy`; with another adapter they are on the State port.

enabledWorkspaces.description: The workspaces the controller may CHANGE (the policy document's `controllers.slack.enabledWorkspaces`), by the key of `access.slack.workspaces`.

recordsDir.description: The console's records, mounted. Read only with `ports.adapter: legacy`.

tokenFile.description: This pod's projected ServiceAccount token, presented to the console and read afresh on every call.

directory.description: The corporate directories this deployment declares: each adopted at start (the console connects the others). Unset declares none.

workspaces.description: The declared workspaces. One that cannot be adopted stops the service.

items.description: A workspace: deliberately thin. Its domains and the tenant's own id are discovered.

id.description: The backend's tenant id. Optional: given, the adoption checks it.

keySecret.description: The secret the service-account key is: `directory/<id>/key`.

serve.description: Narrows the tenant to these domains. Empty serves every domain discovered.

syncGroups.description: Narrows the tenant to these groups. Empty keeps every group in the served domains.

exchange.description: How the token exchange verifies workloads and whom it trusts. `audience` is written to the service document; the clusters, the AWS accounts and the GitHub owners are the policy document's `exchange`.

audience.description: The audience a workload token must be minted for (the service document's `exchange.audience`). Defaults to `release`, so two issuers in one cluster cannot accept each other's proofs.

aws.description: The AWS accounts whose roles' outbound identity tokens (sts:GetWebIdentityToken) are verified. An empty list verifies none.

name.description: The estate's word for it, for logs.

audience.description: The audience the role must request. Required with an account: it is the trust boundary.

maxAge.description: Refuse a token whose `iat` is older than this. At most 1h.

clusters.description: The clusters whose ServiceAccount tokens are verified, each against the key set it publishes for itself. This service's own cluster is a row like any other.

jwksUri.description: Where its keys are. Unset discovers them from the issuer.

name.description: The estate's word for it: the cluster in a `service_account` matcher. Renaming a row changes every rule about it.

github.description: Whose GitHub Actions tokens are verified, for this issuer's URL as the audience.

owners.description: The organisations. None verifies none: an empty list would admit every repository there is.

freshness.description: How the directory's snapshot is kept current.

freshnessWindow.description: How old a snapshot may be and still be answered from.

probeInterval.description: How often the directory is probed.

refreshInterval.description: How often a snapshot is refreshed.

instance.description: The installation's name (`acme`, `prod`): lower-case letters, digits and dashes. Its SSM root is `/sluis/<instance>`, so two installations share an account; `private`, `export`, `internal` and `external` would nest under another's tree.

issuer.description: The issuer and where a browser reaches the console.

consoleURL.description: Where a browser reaches the console, with its mount (`publicURL`). Default `<url>/console`.

groupsScoping.description: How far per-audience `groups` scoping has been taken: `off`, `report` or `enforce` (`groupsScoping`).

secureCookies.description: Mark session cookies Secure (`secureCookies`). Unset follows the https of the URL.

url.description: The issuer (the service document's `issuerURL`): baked into every token and every relying party's trust.

keys.description: Which key serves which purpose. Keys are named by alias (KMS) or by name (transit), never by ARN or key id. See the package documentation of github.com/truvity/sluis/storage/keys.

oneOf.description: An alias such as alias/audit-seal (kms) or a transit key name. An ARN or a key id is refused.

context.description: The encryption context: "default" sends {instance, purpose}; "off" sends none; an object is sent as is.

key.description: An alias such as alias/audit-seal (kms) or a transit key name. An ARN or a key id is refused.

sign.description: Token signing: the symmetric key that wraps a locally generated signing ring, or an asymmetric key that signs directly (deprecated).

keys.title: keys

lifetimes.description: How long what the issuer hands out lives.

absolute.description: A session, at most. Positive, and at least `token`: a session has to end SOMETIME after sign-in, and an access token cannot outlive the session that grants it.

agent.description: The refresh chains of clients the policy marks `session: agent`, such as MCP hosts (docs/decisions/0040). Their chains are held to these instead of `refresh` and `absolute`.

absolute.description: An agent chain, at most, from `auth_time`. Positive, and at most 2160h (90 days).

access.description: The longest an agent client's access or ID token lives. Positive, and at most 1h.

refresh.description: An agent chain's idle limit. Positive, and at most `absolute`.

hold.description: How long a removal is held before it takes effect.

session.description: The console's own session cookie, capped at `absolute`.

login.description: How a person signs in to the console.

directory.description: Sign in with the corporate directory.

forwarded.description: A sign-in an authenticating proxy has already done.

emailHeader.description: The header that carries the signed-in address.

oauthClient.description: The OAuth client registered once with the directory backend: it drives both admin consent and operator sign-in.

id.description: The client id, for a local run. Not a secret.

idKey.description: The key of the id in that Secret.

provider.description: Names the client's secrets: providers/google/<provider>/client-secret, and providers/google/<provider>/client-id unless `id` gives it. One segment of a secret's name.

secretKey.description: The key of the secret in that Secret.

secretName.description: The Kubernetes Secret the client is declared in, which the console shows and cannot change.

openbao.description: An OpenBao the secrets are kept in (the `openbao` secrets adapter, under `root`). Setting it chooses that adapter for `secrets` unless `adapters.secrets` names another. It is an answer to the preset's question: the preset's own answers do not ask for an OpenBao.

address.description: The server, https only and with no path.

auth.description: How the service logs in: a role of the kubernetes or jwt auth method, with a token read from a file.

caFile.description: The PEM bundle the server's certificate chains to.

mount.description: The KV version 2 mount. Default the adapter's.

root.description: The root of the layout inside the mount: `sluis`.

policyFile.description: Where the service finds the policy document (the service document's `policy.file`). Default by shape: `/opt/sluis/policy.yaml` (lambda, the configuration layer), `/var/run/access-issuer/policy/policy.yaml` (kubernetes, where the chart mounts it), `/etc/sluis/policy.yaml` (server).

preset.description: The adapters of a whole platform, one per concern: `server` (no AWS, no Kubernetes), `k8s-minimal`, `k8s-openbao`, `aws-serverless`, `aws-hybrid` (sluis on Lambda, a cluster for the workloads), `k8s-aws` (sluis as a pod on Kubernetes with AWS storage: DynamoDB, S3, KMS-wrapped signing; SSM secrets, or OpenBao with `adapters.secrets`). `aws-eks` is the deprecated name of `k8s-aws`. Absent, the preset the `platform` answers lead to; with neither, the `ports` keys decide. `adapters` and the `ports` keys override single concerns.

recovery.description: The sign-in that needs no directory: in a cluster, a token for a ServiceAccount proven against the API server; anywhere else, a password. Unset is off for the issuer and, for the hub, on.

audience.description: The audience its token must carry.

enabled.description: Turn recovery on. Needs `inCluster`, `serviceAccount` and `audience` to be usable.

passwordSecret.description: Outside a cluster: the secret the recovery password is (`recovery/password`), read at start (the hub keeps only an Argon2id digest of it). Unset generates one and prints it, except on a function, where recovery is then off. `enabled: false` leaves it untouched and refuses the sign-in, so turning it back on needs no new password.

serviceAccount.description: The ServiceAccount whose token signs in.

release.description: The name the installation's objects carry (the service document's `release`). On Kubernetes, the release's full name.

secrets.description: How the secrets this document names are delivered (truvity/policy config.md section 5). Absent is `env`.

endpoint.description: `ssm`: overrides the SSM address, for LocalStack.

grace.description: `ssm`: how long the previous value of a rotated client secret is still accepted: the document's previous revision, while the current one is younger than this (docs/decisions/0039-the-issuer-generates-confidential-client-secrets.md, the overlap).

kmsKeyId.description: `ssm`: the id, ARN or alias of the customer-managed KMS key the parameters the service itself writes (its credentials) are encrypted with. Unset, the AWS-managed `alias/aws/ssm`. The `ssm` secrets adapter's `kmsKeyId` setting; naming another there is refused.

layout.description: `ssm`: the storage layout of the installation's secrets: `v4`, the only one and the default. It keeps them under `<root>/internal/` and `<root>/external/` (docs/decisions/0041-the-secret-contract.md). Layouts v3 and `transition` are gone; an installation still on one runs v1.74.x and `sluis migrate secrets-layout` first.

refresh.description: `ssm`: how old a secret's copy may be before it is read again: a rotated secret reaches every instance within it.

region.description: `ssm`: the region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

root.description: `file`: the directory the secrets are mounted under. `ssm`: the installation's root, /sluis/<instance>.

source.description: `env`: the variable SLUIS_SECRET_<NAME> (the name upper-cased, every other character an underscore), for a local run. `file`: the file <root>/<name>, read on every use, so a rotated mount takes effect without a restart. `ssm`: the SecureString <root>/internal/config/<name> in AWS SSM Parameter Store, every one under the prefix read at once and again after `refresh` (root /sluis/<instance>).

shape.description: Where the installation runs: `lambda` (one AWS Lambda function), `kubernetes` (one Deployment) or `server` (one process). It fixes the paths the documents name and what is derived.

signingKey.description: The issuer's signing keys: provisioned, never minted here.

activationDelay.description: How long a newly published key waits before a replica signs with it. At least `pollInterval`.

additionalFiles.description: Every OTHER algorithm this installation signs with at once, one file per algorithm.

file.description: The primary key. Unset generates one for this process, which a local run may do and nothing else should. Exclusive with `kms`.

kms.description: Sign with AWS KMS keys instead of a file: the private key never leaves KMS. Exclusive with `file`.

additional.description: Every OTHER algorithm this installation signs with at once, each on its own rotation track, as `signingKey.additionalFiles` does for files. RS256 is the one that exists: for relying parties that need it (Kargo, EKS's OIDC provider).

keys.description: RSA_2048, RSA_3072 or RSA_4096 SIGN_VERIFY keys, oldest first, the last signing; same rotation rules as `keys`.

ECC_NIST_P384 SIGN_VERIFY keys, as ids, ARNs or aliases, oldest first. The LAST signs; the earlier ones stay published until `overlap` after the next one activates. Rotation appends a key. The role needs kms:Sign and kms:GetPublicKey on each.

region.description: The keys' region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

stateSecret.description: The secret (`issuer/state-secret`) holding at least 32 random bytes as base64 or hex (`openssl rand -base64 32`), the same in every replica (a replica whose secret differs refuses to start), from which the sign-in state is derived: a KMS key has no private bytes to derive from.

kmsWrapped.description: Sign with key pairs AWS KMS generates and wraps under ONE symmetric key (the `kms-wrapped` adapter): a new pair per algorithm every `rotateEvery`, published before it signs and kept after it is replaced. The private key is decrypted into process memory to sign. Exclusive with `file` and `kms`.

algorithms.description: The algorithms signed with, the first the installation default. Unset is ES384 and RS256. EdDSA is not supported yet.

keyId.description: DEPRECATED, accepted for one release with a warning: name the symmetric key as `keys.sign` instead. An alias given here is mapped onto `keys.sign`; an ARN or an id is refused.

prepublish.description: How long a new key is published before anything signs with it: longer than a verifier caches the key set (Envoy's jwt_authn: 10m). Unset is `activationDelay`.

region.description: The key's region. Unset follows the AWS SDK's own resolution.

retain.description: How long a replaced key stays published: at least `lifetimes.token` plus a skew margin. Unset is `overlap`.

rotateEvery.description: How often a new key pair is generated for each algorithm. Longer than `prepublish`, at most 168h.

stateSecret.description: The secret (`issuer/state-secret`) holding at least 32 random bytes as base64 or hex, the same in every replica, from which the sign-in state is derived: a wrapped key is replaced daily and the state must outlive it.

overlap.description: How long a rotated key stays published. Unset is `lifetimes.token` plus a margin for clock skew.

pollInterval.description: How often the files are re-read.

verifyOnly.description: PUBLIC keys published in the JWKS and never signed with, so tokens an earlier signer issued keep verifying until they expire: the overlap of a cutover from file keys to `kmsWrapped`. Each is dropped from the JWKS at its `until`. A private key stops the start.

alg.description: The key's algorithm. Unset follows the key.

file.description: A PEM public key (`PUBLIC KEY`, `RSA PUBLIC KEY`, or a certificate) or a JWK file. Never a private key.

kid.description: The `kid` the old tokens carry. Unset is the RFC 7638 thumbprint of the key, which is what a file signer derived for it.

until.description: An RFC 3339 instant after which the key is no longer published: the old tokens' last expiry, plus the verifiers' cache. Required: an overlap has an end.

valkey.description: Deprecated in v1.74.0, removed in v1.75: migrate with `sluis migrate`. The shared store for logins in progress and snapshots. Unset keeps both in memory, correct for one replica.

cluster.description: Speak the cluster protocol. A plain single server needs it off.

passwordSecret.description: The secret the password is (`valkey/password`). Unset connects with none.
